pr.title: Draw the band's divider at full strength
pr.head: e23d61c57a97caad0918318a19b5b5a1a825e24d

summary: Projector's plugin draws a band above Claude Code's prompt: a short list of the session's open pull requests, questions, and notices. In a terminal, the band's first line is its divider, a rule of ─ characters across the band's width that ends in how long ago the band reloaded, such as updated just now. Claude Code draws the band's [-] collapse mark just past the divider's end.

Until this change, the divider took the theme's subtle color, the muted color the band also uses for a row's details, such as its author and age. So the band's top edge and its update time read as muted text. The owner wants that line at full strength, so this change drops the color from the divider and lets it draw in the terminal's default text color. Every other muted part of the band keeps subtle.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Band: the plugin's panel above Claude Code's prompt, built in hooks/register.tsx.
  • Divider: the band's first line in a terminal, a rule that ends in the time since the band reloaded.
  • subtle: the theme color the band uses for muted text. The band uses it in place of dimColor, which does not dim in every terminal.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review of this head found it clean, with no finding threads.

groups.title: The divider loses its muted color
groups.kicker: One prop removed from the divider, and the test that pins it
intro: The divider is a <Text key="divider"> element that register builds once per render, only when the band draws in a terminal. Both the empty band and the band with rows put the same element first, so one edit changes the divider everywhere it appears.

The test that draws the band's rows used to assert that the divider's color is subtle. It now asserts that the divider sets neither color nor dimColor, so a later change that mutes the divider again fails it.

files.note: Builds the band. The divider element drops color="subtle".

checks.text: Only the divider changes. The loading line, the tagline, and each row's author, age, and details still set color="subtle", as a search of the file at this head shows.

files.note: The band's row test now asserts that the divider carries no color and no dimColor.

checks.text: The test finds the divider by its text, a run of ─ ending in updated just now or updated Ns ago, so it reads the props of the real divider element.
